signals.title: USD/JPY — Geopolitical Risk + BoJ Intervention + Options Skew
signals.text: USD/JPY trades at 163.51, holding above its SMA20/50/200 cluster following a naval mine blast in the Strait of Hormuz. Despite the geopolitical shock, a 275bp Fed-BoJ carry differential continues to anchor the pair's upside while JPY COT leverage net shorts remain extreme at -114,030 (26.7% long). The 25d Risk Reversal (Saxo) at -1.48 shows a moderate put skew, signaling that the options market is paying for downside protection against potential BoJ intervention as price stays elevated. Retail sentiment is also at a 14% long / 86% short extreme, creating a contrarian risk of further squeeze if the 163.79 resistance holds. High-impact headlines regarding a US-Iran strike pause provide a temporary ceiling, but the carry advantage remains the dominant structural driver. Risk: A breach of 165.00 triggers direct BoJ intervention, forcing a rapid liquidation of the crowded spec short.

signals.title: AUD/USD — OIS Carry + Volatility Premium + Technicals
signals.text: AUD/USD is testing 0.7003, positioned above its SMA20 (0.6957) and SMA200 (0.6901) but capped by the SMA50 at 0.7027. The pair is supported by a -71bp OIS carry premium favoring the AUD as the RBA remains on hold at 4.35% while the Fed sits at 3.75%. Options pricing shows significant concern regarding future realized moves, with an ATM IV of 13.9% vs an HV30 of 6.1%, resulting in a massive +7.8% Vol Risk Premium. COT data confirms speculative conviction with a net long position of +20,521 (62.8% long), while the 25d Risk Reversal at -0.90 suggests traders are hedging for AUD weakness despite the spot bid. This divergence indicates institutional caution at the 0.7000 handle. Risk: A close below the SMA20 at 0.6957 invalidates the bullish structure and triggers a long-liquidation toward 0.6901.

signals.title: NZD/USD — ESI Divergence + Positioning Extreme
signals.text: NZD/USD trades at 0.5799, struggling at the SMA50 resistance of 0.5796 despite a Strong Positive Economic Surprise Index (ESI) of +22.2. RBNZ holds at 2.5%. The negative real rate of -1.56% in New Zealand (2.5% rate vs 4.06% inflation expectations) remains the primary fundamental drag, but the data outperformance suggests the fundamental floor is higher than current pricing. Retail sentiment at 66% long confirms that smaller participants are already attempting to catch the reversal, which often delays the move. Watch for a sustained break above 0.5824 (SMA200) to confirm the squeeze. Risk: RBNZ pivots to a hold at the September 2nd meeting, validating the existing spec short.

signals.title: EUR/USD — ESI Underperformance + Volatility Premium
signals.text: EUR/USD trades at 1.1413, currently pinned below its SMA20 (1.1419) and the broader SMA cluster. The Eurozone Economic Surprise Index (ESI) shows a moderate negative bias at -14.6, as data continues to miss expectations relative to the US. While the ECB is in a hiking cycle at 2.4%, the 146bp OIS carry disadvantage against the USD (3.64%) limits upside potential in a bull flattener yield regime. The options market is pricing in risk with a +2.5% Vol Risk Premium (IV 7.1% vs HV30 4.6%) and a mild put skew in the 25d Risk Reversals (-0.49). Speculative positioning is already heavily net short at -80,570, suggesting that much of the bearish narrative is priced in, yet no catalyst for a reversal has emerged. Risk: A hawkish ECB surprise on September 10th forces a squeeze of the net short position toward the SMA200 at 1.1639.
